title: Did People in the Bible Really Live 900 Years

shots.line: Methuselah lived nine hundred and sixty-nine years.
shots.scene: ancient Methuselah, bent over his cane in a pre-flood valley; 969 burns into the sky

shots.line: And if you add up the numbers in Genesis...
shots.scene: on parchment the numbers add up: 187 + 182 + 600 = 969

shots.line: he died in the very same year the Flood came.
shots.scene: the Flood: the ark in towering waves — 'the very same year'

shots.line: Adam lived nine hundred and thirty years.
shots.scene: old Adam, white beard, outside Eden — 930

shots.line: Noah, nine hundred and fifty.
shots.scene: Noah before the ark on the mountain — 950

shots.line: Today, almost no one reaches one hundred.
shots.scene: today: an old man blows at a cake with 100 candles — a modern room

shots.line: So either the Bible got its numbers wrong...
shots.scene: the numbers on the scroll flicker — a red question mark

shots.line: or something happened to the human race.
shots.scene: dusk: generations walking into the distance, each smaller than the last

shots.line: Something we have forgotten.
shots.scene: close: Methuselah's ancient eyes look up — something forgotten

shots.line: DID THEY REALLY LIVE 900 YEARS?
shots.scene: aerial of the pre-flood world, title DID THEY REALLY LIVE 900 YEARS?

shots.line: It is all written in Genesis chapter five.
shots.scene: aerial: glide over the villages of the first generations

shots.line: A family tree that reads like a list of impossible birthdays. Adam, nine hundred and thirty. Seth, nine hundred and twelve. Enosh, nine hundred and five. Jared, nine hundred and sixty-two.
shots.scene: the Genesis 5 family tree unrolls, ages appearing line by line

shots.line: And Methuselah, the oldest man who ever lived.
shots.scene: Methuselah close-up: 969 — THE OLDEST MAN WHO EVER LIVED

shots.line: Every name comes with an exact age.
shots.scene: every name — an exact age (scroll, names highlighted)

shots.line: The age he became a father.
shots.scene: the age he became a father (column highlighted)

shots.line: And the age he died.
shots.scene: and the age he died (column highlighted)

shots.line: This is not written like a fairy tale.
shots.scene: a storybook opens 'ONCE UPON A TIME…' — stamped ✗

shots.line: It is written like a record.
shots.scene: the family tree with a seal: A RECORD

shots.line: So what is going on?
shots.scene: Adam (old) scratches his head — so what is going on?

shots.line: The most popular answer online is simple.
shots.scene: a phone full of comments: 'they counted months!'

shots.line: It is a mistranslation.
shots.scene: MISTRANSLATION?

shots.line: They were counting months, not years.
shots.scene: calendar pages flip: MONTHS, not years

shots.line: Nine hundred and thirty months is about seventy-seven years.
shots.scene: 930 MONTHS → 77 YEARS

shots.line: Perfectly normal.
shots.scene: a perfectly normal 77-year-old Adam, smiling

shots.line: Problem solved?
shots.scene: green stamp: SOLVED?

shots.line: Not so fast.
shots.scene: record scratch — the stamp cracks and turns red: NOT SO FAST

shots.line: Look at Enoch.
shots.scene: meet Enoch, walking in the hills

shots.line: Genesis says Enoch became a father at sixty-five.
shots.scene: Enoch holds his newborn son — father at 65

shots.line: If those are months...
shots.scene: IF those are months: calendar 65 MONTHS

shots.line: Enoch was five years old.
shots.scene: Enoch shrinks into a five-year-old boy holding a baby

shots.line: And Mahalalel?
shots.scene: and Mahalalel?

shots.line: Also a father at sixty-five.
shots.scene: Mahalalel — also a father at 65

shots.line: A five-year-old dad.
shots.scene: two five-year-old dads, each holding a baby, looking at each other

shots.line: The month theory doesn't fix the problem.
shots.scene: the calendar gets a big red ✗

shots.line: It creates a bigger one.
shots.scene: cracks spread across the calendar — a bigger problem

shots.line: And the Hebrew word used here is shanah.
shots.scene: the Hebrew word: שָׁנָה SHANAH

shots.line: It means year.
shots.scene: SHANAH = YEAR

shots.line: The same word used for every other year in the Bible.
shots.scene: the same word glowing again and again across a long scroll

shots.line: Myth number one. Busted.
shots.scene: MYTH #1: BUSTED — big stamp

shots.line: So maybe the numbers were borrowed.
shots.scene: numbers float from a clay tablet onto the scroll — borrowed?

shots.line: Skeptics point to an ancient clay tablet from Mesopotamia.
shots.scene: aerial Mesopotamia: the Euphrates, a stepped ziggurat, a mud-brick city, palms

shots.line: The Sumerian King List.
shots.scene: the clay tablet: THE SUMERIAN KING LIST

shots.line: It names eight kings who ruled before a great flood.
shots.scene: eight Sumerian kings with tall golden hats line up before a ziggurat

shots.line: And their reigns are insane.
shots.scene: close: a Sumerian king, very pleased with himself — INSANE reigns

shots.line: One king ruled for twenty-eight thousand, eight hundred years.
shots.scene: tablet row lights up: ALULIM — 28,800 YEARS

shots.line: Another, for thirty-six thousand.
shots.scene: ALALNGAR — 36,000 YEARS

shots.line: Together, those eight kings ruled for over two hundred and forty thousand years.
shots.scene: all eight rows fill in; a counter races to 241,200 years

shots.line: And then the flood came.
shots.scene: aerial: the whole world is water — the ark alone under storm clouds

shots.line: After the flood, the reigns suddenly shrink.
shots.scene: after the flood the tablet's numbers shrink: 1,500 … 420 … 126

shots.line: Sound familiar?
shots.scene: split: the clay tablet beside the Genesis scroll — sound familiar?

shots.line: Two completely different cultures.
shots.scene: a Sumerian scribe and a Hebrew elder face each other across a river

shots.line: Both remember long-lived ancestors.
shots.scene: both remember long-lived ancestors — ancient elders appear behind each

shots.line: Both remember a flood.
shots.scene: both remember a flood — the storm sea rises

shots.line: And both remember lifespans collapsing after it.
shots.scene: both remember lifespans collapsing — a quick chart drop

shots.line: But notice the difference.
shots.scene: push in between tablet and scroll: notice the difference

shots.line: The Sumerian numbers are fantasy.
shots.scene: the tablet's giant numbers — stamped FANTASY

shots.line: The Bible's numbers are strangely restrained.
shots.scene: the Genesis scroll by comparison: calm, restrained numbers

shots.line: Not thousands of years.
shots.scene: NOT THOUSANDS OF YEARS

shots.line: Not tens of thousands.
shots.scene: NOT TENS OF THOUSANDS

shots.line: Under one thousand, every single time.
shots.scene: chart: every pre-flood bar stays under a glowing 1,000 line

shots.line: Maybe this is not one story copying another.
shots.scene: a copying arrow from tablet to scroll gets crossed out

shots.line: Maybe it is two memories of the same event.
shots.scene: both the tablet and the scroll point to one image: the ark on the waters

shots.line: So what was different back then?
shots.scene: the pre-flood valley at dawn, giant trees, mist

shots.line: Genesis describes a world we would not recognize.
shots.scene: a world we would not recognize: enormous trees, strange light, a shimmering sky

shots.line: Waters above the sky.
shots.scene: WATERS ABOVE THE SKY — a shimmering water layer arches over the clouds

shots.line: The fountains of the great deep, still sealed.
shots.scene: cross-section of the earth: sealed underground water chambers

shots.line: Some believe a thick layer of water vapor once shielded the earth.
shots.scene: the earth from space wrapped in a shimmering vapor canopy

shots.line: Less radiation. A gentler climate.
shots.scene: radiation rays strike the canopy and bounce off — gentler climate

shots.line: Others believe the first humans simply had near-perfect genes.
shots.scene: a glowing golden DNA helix — near-perfect genes

shots.line: Fewer mutations. Bodies that could repair themselves for centuries.
shots.scene: tiny repair sparks fix the helix — fewer mutations, bodies that repair themselves

shots.line: These ideas are debated, even among believers.
shots.scene: two scholars argue over the theories by lamplight

shots.line: But one thing is not debated.
shots.scene: BUT ONE THING IS NOT DEBATED

shots.line: The numbers change after the Flood.
shots.scene: aerial: the ark resting high on snowy mountains as the water recedes

shots.line: Watch what happens.
shots.scene: an empty chart: watch what happens

shots.line: Noah, nine hundred and fifty.
shots.scene: bar: NOAH 950

shots.line: His son Shem, six hundred.
shots.scene: bar: SHEM 600

shots.line: A few generations later, four hundred.
shots.scene: bars: ~400

shots.line: Then two hundred and thirty.
shots.scene: bars: ~230

shots.line: Abraham, one hundred and seventy-five.
shots.scene: aerial Canaan: rolling hills, Abraham's tent camp, flocks of sheep

shots.line: Joseph, one hundred and ten.
shots.scene: aerial Egypt: the Nile, fields, palms, pyramids

shots.line: Moses, one hundred and twenty.
shots.scene: aerial from Mount Nebo over the Jordan valley and the promised land

shots.line: And a few centuries later, the psalm says...
shots.scene: old Moses writes a psalm by lamplight (Psalm 90 is 'a prayer of Moses')

shots.line: "The years of our life are seventy, or even by reason of strength eighty."
shots.scene: "The years of our life are seventy, or even by reason of strength eighty"

shots.line: That is not random.
shots.scene: the full chart with all bars: not random

shots.line: It is a curve.
shots.scene: a red dashed curve draws across the tops of the bars: IT'S A CURVE

shots.line: A steady, downward decline.
shots.scene: the curve glows: a steady, downward decline

shots.line: Exactly what you would expect if something in humanity was breaking down.
shots.scene: an hourglass running out, cracks spreading in the glass — something breaking down

shots.line: And there is one more verse that changes everything.
shots.scene: the scroll glows: one more verse

shots.line: Genesis six, verse three.
shots.scene: GENESIS 6:3

shots.line: Before the Flood, God says...
shots.scene: before the flood: light breaks over the dark pre-flood world as God speaks

shots.line: "My Spirit shall not abide in man forever... his days shall be one hundred and twenty years."
shots.scene: "My Spirit shall not abide in man forever… his days shall be 120 years"

shots.line: Many read this as a countdown to the Flood.
shots.scene: Noah hammers at the half-built ark; an hourglass labelled 120 YEARS

shots.line: Others read it as a new limit on human life.
shots.scene: or a new limit: a red 120 line across the lifespan chart

shots.line: Now here is the strange part.
shots.scene: NOW HERE IS THE STRANGE PART

shots.line: The oldest person ever verified by modern science...
shots.scene: a certificate: OLDEST VERIFIED HUMAN

shots.line: was a French woman named Jeanne Calment.
shots.scene: Jeanne Calment, white hair and glasses, smiling in her armchair-room

shots.line: She died at one hundred and twenty-two.
shots.scene: her cake reads 122

shots.line: In thousands of years of records...
shots.scene: chart: the 120 line, record-holders clustered just below it

shots.line: no one has broken the limit by more than a breath.
shots.scene: the 120 limit line glows — no one has broken it by more than a breath

shots.line: So, did they really live nine hundred years?
shots.scene: the verdict board

shots.line: Mistranslation? The text says years, and the math breaks if it does not.
shots.scene: row 1: mistranslation — BUSTED

shots.line: Copied from a myth? The Bible's account is far more restrained than the myths around it.
shots.scene: row 2: copied myth — far more restrained

shots.line: Literal? The text certainly presents itself that way.
shots.scene: row 3: literal — the text presents itself that way

shots.line: And the steady decline after the Flood fits that story.
shots.scene: row 4: the decline fits the story

shots.line: But the real question is not how long they lived.
shots.scene: BUT THE REAL QUESTION…

shots.line: It is why they died at all.
shots.scene: close: old Adam, eyes heavy — why did they die at all?

shots.line: In the beginning, death was not part of the plan.
shots.scene: Eden in perfect light: death was never part of the plan

shots.line: Adam was made to live.
shots.scene: young Adam stands beside the tree of life, glowing

shots.line: The tree of life stood in the middle of the garden.
shots.scene: aerial: Eden, the great tree of life at the centre of the four rivers

shots.line: But when sin entered the world, death came with it.
shots.scene: dusk: the bitten fruit falls, leaves wither, Adam and Eve walk away

shots.line: Nine hundred and thirty years was not a superpower.
shots.scene: old Adam on his cane: 930 was not a superpower

shots.line: It was what remained of something much greater.
shots.scene: behind old Adam, a ghostly glowing tree of life fades — what remained of something greater

shots.line: And the Bible ends where it began.
shots.scene: a great book turns from Genesis to Revelation

shots.line: With a tree of life.
shots.scene: the heavenly city: a radiant tree of life beside a crystal river

shots.line: And a promise.
shots.scene: light pours down: a promise

shots.line: "Death shall be no more."
shots.scene: "Death shall be no more."

shots.line: Not nine hundred years. Forever.
shots.scene: final: the tree of life in golden light — NOT 900 YEARS. FOREVER.
